nodes.label: FlatAim Laser Bolt Facing-Axis Fix
nodes.rationale: First reflection-style patch for the visible-projectile rotation was wrong; the actual bug was a heading-axis convention mismatch: FlatAim aim heading uses atan2(x,y) from +Y while KEX object facing needs atan2(y,x) from +X. Fixed via SS2FA_DirToProjectileObjectFacing().

nodes.label: FlatAim Wrench/Melee Viewmodel Implementation
nodes.rationale: Added SS2FAMeleeViewmodel extends NDShockMeleeViewmodel to retarget PlyrArm from FlatAim view-frame aim after native melee update runs, letting Wrench and other melee weapons track the FlatAim crosshair.

nodes.label: FlatAim Melee Orientation-Mode Investigation
nodes.rationale: Multi-step debugging arc for melee aim-follow: direct proxy-facing writes to PlyrArm (mode 2) made the Wrench disappear on F5; native-relative heading/bank writes caused rapid spin/orbit; the eventual mode 3 fix writes no PlyrArm facing at all and follows the reticle via camera-screen-plane location offset only, using point-rig local-frame axes (X=forward, Y=left, Z=up) rather than gun-proxy axes.

nodes.label: FlatAim Pickup Reach Regression
nodes.rationale: FreeAim pickup range appeared extended versus stock; root cause was a stale selection_semantic_reach=20.0 override in flataim.ini left over from earlier selection tuning, while the compiled fallback and stock frob reach were both 8 KEX units.

nodes.label: FlatAim Ultrawide Overlay-Canvas Coordinate Bug
nodes.rationale: At 3440x1440 the crosshair started off-center. Root cause: Squirrel ShockOverlay code used Engine.GetCanvasSize()/2, correct only at 1920x1080 where it happens to equal the fixed 960x540 overlay canvas. Two more iterations were needed: a fixed-960x540 fix still snapped left until a hidden native HUD-origin bias was disabled; final fix treats ShockOverlay as height-normalized (hudY=540, hudX=rawW*540/rawH).

nodes.label: FlatAim Dynamic Canvas Sizing
nodes.rationale: Initial Freelook crosshair position behaved as if 1920x1080 was baked in at other resolutions. Fixed by publishing the live KEX canvas size (ss2fa_canvas) from Engine.GetCanvasSize() through the config bridge, which in turn exposed the separate overlay-canvas coordinate-space bug.

nodes.label: FlatAim Edge-Pan View Follow
nodes.rationale: Adds view movement as the freeaim cursor nears the screen edge; writes synthetic native yaw/pitch accumulators and calls native PlayerTurnTilt when the reticle enters an edge band, ramped by proximity to the edge.

nodes.label: Left-Hand Additive Model Material-Invisibility Investigation
nodes.rationale: Investigation of why candidate left-hand models (ss2vr_lk, ss2vr_lj, ss2vr_lm, ss2vr_ln) failed to render visibly despite reaching the additive viewmodel render path. ss2vr_lk rendered but contributed no visible pixels (lit-stack problem); ss2vr_lm was invisible; ss2vr_ln crashed AE. A compact-vs-five-slot material-table A/B found no safe lit path, so the known-visible flatlit ss2vr_ls fallback was restored as default, with lj/lk/lm/ln parked behind a redirect guard pending a RenderDoc A/B against the stock hand.

nodes.label: Left-Hand Pose-Loss Hide Confound
nodes.rationale: Early left-hand material tests were confounded by ss2vr_lhand_hide_on_pose_loss=1 destroying/hiding the additive hand before creation whenever the left controller pose was invalid, masking whether the underlying material/BIN was the real problem.

nodes.label: Vanilla Gamepad Analog Injector Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY pursued initially: physical-controller analog movement/view failure in vanilla SS2:AE (without the SS2VR injector) was suspected to be a KEX cvar/injector-path problem, prompting an experimental native_axis_direct workaround. ROOT CAUSE actually found: a stale joystick_enable 0 line in user.bnd, synced and persisted across reinstalls/PCs by Steam Cloud, disabled the legacy joystick axis consumer. Fixing that line restored physical-controller analog input in vanilla AE with no injector change needed.

nodes.label: SS2VR native_axis_direct Experimental Input Path
nodes.rationale: Release-DLL experimental path (behind [motion_controls] native_axis_direct=true) that signature-checks and calls the game's native forward/sidestep input-binder handlers directly on the game thread; built while the vanilla gamepad failure was still misattributed to the injector, and became unnecessary once the user.bnd/Steam Cloud root cause was found.

nodes.label: Frob Target Library (Archetype Family Policy)
nodes.rationale: Design principle: a VR frob/physics-grab target selector should not use a per-instance object-id list. It should gate on FrobInfo/BlockFrob plus archetype-family checks (Object.InheritsFrom for Usable Containers, Controllers, Decorative, Computers, Keys, Corpses, etc.), with name hints only as fallback. Captured in docs/FROB_TARGET_LIBRARY.md as an evolving allow/deny policy.

nodes.label: Debug informationTracker Overlay State Oracle
nodes.rationale: AE's in-game informationTracker debug panel exposes a live human-readable true/false list of the same native HUD overlay flags SS2VR reads from gOverlayOn[50]. Useful as a fast oracle for comparing against right_arm_hud/floating-panel state, though it does not replace gOverlayRects[50] or D3D draw classification for per-panel textures.

nodes.label: FunkMaxExport 3ds Max Export Tool
nodes.rationale: 3ds Max GUI/Python tool suite (versions v0.6.2 through v0.6.44+ across this range) for round-tripping SS2:AE LGMD/LGMM/LGPMNM weapon and viewmodel meshes: LGMD Modify Existing (source-preserving edits), LGMD Custom (fresh static geometry), Import LGMM Ref, Import LGPMNM, LGPMNM -> LGMD, and Package KPF.

nodes.label: LGMD/LGMM/LGPMNM Mesh Format Family
nodes.rationale: LGMD is the static/animated viewmodel mesh format used by gun and static weapon carriers. LGMM is a separate skeletal/AI mesh format (needs companion .CAL joint data) used by melee arm rigs like pipewrench_h.bin/wrench_h.bin; direct LGMM export is not implemented, so LGMM sources are converted through FreeTheObjects into referenceable geometry instead. LGPMNM is a high-detail mesh payload embedded inside some LGMM/LGMD files.

nodes.label: LGPMNM Embedded High-Detail Mesh Discovery
nodes.rationale: Discovered that pipewrench_h.bin and wrench_h.bin embed a high-detail LGPMNM payload after the classic low-poly LGMM core (materials ND-melee_arm.psd plus wrench-specific slots), explaining why FunkMax's classic LGMM importer only ever produced the low-poly arm. The same payload family (short PMNM-wrapper form, missing the LG prefix) was later found in rapier_h.bin, psword_h.bin, and shard_h.bin.

nodes.label: Animated Hand-Husk Crash Investigation
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage misdiagnosis arc for weapon-equip crashes after hand-removal trims. Stage 1 (WRONG): zero-face animated hand subobjects (@s01_han etc.) were assumed safe if parse-clean; a safe-stub exporter converted them to one-face hidden stubs. Stage 2 (falsified): one-face husks still crashed on weapon-switch in headset even though mouse-wheel switching outside VR looked fine; the validator was extended to block near-empty (<=1 face) animated hand/han subobjects and pistol/AR/laser overrides were pulled back to stock fallback. Stage 3 (resolution): specific one-face hand-stub BINs were live-proven per weapon and allowlisted by exact SHA256 rather than by a general structural rule.

nodes.label: Stale LGMD Light/Normal Aux-Range Bug
nodes.rationale: After face deletion, source-preserving LGMD exports (shotgun, EMP) kept the original stale subobject light/normal record ranges even though far fewer records were actually referenced by the remaining faces, unlike stock LGMDs which have exact contiguous ranges. Fixed by an auxcompact pass that compacts lights/normals together with faces/nodes.

nodes.label: Stale LGMD v4 Material-Extras/Tail Bug
nodes.rationale: The earlier fix of zeroing v4 material-extra header fields on source-preserving exports was itself wrong: vanilla LGMDs keep populated material-extra fields (material_offset + 26*num_materials pattern) and a correct v4 end offset. Zeroing them mismatched the still-present aux material bytes and left a stale end-offset pointing at the original larger stock file size. Fixed by repairing/repointing extras and the end offset instead of zeroing, with the validator extended to fail zeroed/stale v4 tails.

nodes.label: Custom .mtl Include-Chain Crash
nodes.rationale: Packaging custom .mtl sidecars with include statements (e.g. ../../materials/ND-viewmodel.inc) caused a null-read AV crash on save-load, matching an earlier pattern seen with ss2vr_lj. Fixed by rewriting the .mtl files as fully inline material scripts with no include lines.

nodes.label: AR15 Custom-Vhot Loader Crash Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: adding custom high-ID vhots (80/81/82) to the live-good AR15 crashed KEX's native LGMD loader before menu, first attributed to high/non-contiguous vhot IDs; remapping to low IDs (2/3/4) still crashed identically, falsifying that theory. ROOT CAUSE (Ghidra plus stock comparison): LGMD header byte 68 (num_vhots) was stale, left at 2 even though 5 vhot records were written; stock sg_h.bin's byte 68=3 matches its 3 vhots. Fixed by rewriting header bytes 66..69 during rebuild and adding a validator check for stale header counts.

nodes.label: Stale LGMD Header Count Confound (ss2vr_wrench_h)
nodes.rationale: After the byte-68 AR15 fix, a retest still crashed, but crash-dump/KPF forensics showed the installed package did not even contain the patched AR15 - the real active suspect was a stale header vhot/subobject count on an unrelated static viewmodel (ss2vr_wrench_h, byte 69 num_subobjects stale) entering the same native vhot-builder path. Repairing header counts on all custom ss2vr_* static assets, not just the AR15, let the save load and proved the AR15 vhot fix was viable all along.

nodes.label: Weapon-Equip INT3 Crash: Zero-Face Animated Subobjects
nodes.rationale: Root-caused via crashlog (BREAKPOINT at SystemShock2Remastered.exe+0x94EBCB, in-memory LGMD name Grip00C) to the pistol viewmodel override obj/atek_h.bin retaining two animated zero-face hand subobjects (@s01_han, @s02_han); the same pattern existed in parked ss2vr_assault_rifle.bin and ss2vr_lasehand.bin. Fixed short-term by removing the risky stock-name overrides and gating any future model swap behind an explicit unsafe flag, plus a new validate_lgmd_runtime_safety.py check.

nodes.label: One-Face Hand-Stub Live-Proof Ladder
nodes.rationale: Per-weapon incremental live-testing strategy after the general one-face-stub theory was falsified: test pistol alone (v1.90, accepted SHA 33AF51F8...), then AR15 alone (v1.91, live-good), then laser pistol alone (v1.92, live-good), each promoted to the validator's exact-SHA allowlist only after headset-confirmed stability, rather than trusting a general structural rule.

nodes.label: Static Wrench LGPMNM Export Visual-Fix Saga
nodes.rationale: Iterative visual-correctness pass on the LGPMNM-derived static wrench+hand carrier (ss2vr_wrench_h.bin) after it first rendered but looked too small, rotated, dark, and faceted: principal-length check showed apparent half-size was a carrier scale/pivot illusion, not literal geometry scaling; smoothing-group-aware packed light-normal generation fixed faceted shading; LGPMNM material alpha/emission metadata preservation fixed lost self-illumination on ND-wrench_il.psd; a final packed light-normal inversion (rolled into v0.6.30-lgpmnmlightfix) fixed lighting appearing on the wrong side of the mesh.

nodes.label: Shotgun Animated-Pump Vhot Crash
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: adding vhots to the shotgun caused an equip crash, initially treated as evidence that extra vhots were unsafe on this weapon even though the exported BIN passed strict structural validation. ROOT CAUSE: the vhot export had gone through LGMD Custom instead of LGMD Modify Existing, which renamed/reshaped the animated pump subobject (@00sli.0 -> @00sli_0, vertex range and face count changed); AE's Hybrid_Shotgun animations drive JointPos Joint 1 on that exact subobject identity/range, so altering it broke the animated pump binding. Fixed by re-exporting as a true vhot-only edit over the live-good base via LGMD Modify Existing, preserving the stock subobject name and vertex ranges exactly.

nodes.label: Weapon-Mesh Hand-Removal Trim Package
nodes.rationale: Initial batch of left-hand-removed weapon mesh exports (shotgun, AR15, EMP/shock rifle) prepared for headset testing; shotgun and AR15 preserved their vhots/subobject rig structure with hand faces emptied, while the first EMP export was found geometry-identical to stock and not yet useful. This trim work is what first exposed the animated-hand-husk crash class.

nodes.label: VR Grip/Reload Vhot Authoring Workflow
nodes.rationale: Tooling and convention for authoring motion-controller pivot/grip/reload markers directly in weapon LGMDs: adopted high-ID convention (80=pivot, 81=support grip, 82=reload) which later had to be remapped to low IDs after the header-count crash was found; required several FunkMax fixes for duplicate hidden vhot-id properties on cloned helpers, preserving accepted one-face hand stubs during vhot-only re-exports, skipping near-zero float-roundoff vertex deltas so metadata-only edits stay recognized as such, and baking LGPMNM static vhots in world/snapshot space so exported positions match the Max scene.

nodes.label: Rapier LGPMNM Static Vhot Test
nodes.rationale: Static-carrier LGPMNM export of the rapier (ss2vr_rapier_h.bin) with grip/support vhots, following the same LGPMNM -> LGMD static-snapshot pattern proven on the wrench; must remain a separate obj/ss2vr_rapier_h.bin carrier rather than replacing the stock animated mesh/rapier_h.bin path, since deploying the static mesh over the stock animated melee slot was an earlier crash class.

nodes.label: EMP Rifle Right-Hand Merged Vhot Test
nodes.rationale: Experimental merged-geometry export attaching a right-arm mesh directly onto the EMP rifle model with grip/reload vhots, built via LGMD Custom since the merge adds new topology that LGMD Modify Existing/Nemyax prune workflows cannot handle (they are face-deletion/vhot/move only). Iterated across three test revisions to fix a hand-texture-stretched-across-the-gun material split and restore the stock ND-empgun.psd emission=1.0 self-lit slot.

nodes.label: validate_lgmd_runtime_safety.py Validator
nodes.rationale: CLI validator for exported LGMD BINs, extended repeatedly across this range as new crash classes were discovered: near-empty (<=1 face) animated hand/han subobjects, stale subobject light/normal aux ranges, zeroed/stale v4 material-extras and end-offset tails, stale header vhot/subobject counts (bytes 66..69), duplicate/self-referencing subobject hierarchy links, and an exact-SHA allowlist for live-proven one-face hand-stub weapons.
